s: valley of Jehoshaphat is site of day of the LORD (where the LORD sits to judge)
q: come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat; for there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.

s: Judah will be inhabited forever (future state)
q: But Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.

s: Jerusalem will be inhabited from generation to generation (future state)
q: But Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.

s: Jerusalem will be holy (no strangers will pass through her)
q: Then Jerusalem will be holy, and no strangers will pass through her any more.

s: Israel is heritage of LORD (his people and heritage)
q: for my people, and for my heritage, Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations.

s: The Song of Solomon has title The Song of Solomon
The Song of Solomon has date -0299/-0199
The Song of Solomon has source class canonical
Beloved has complexion dark (also described as lovely)
q: I am dark, but lovely, you daughters of Jerusalem, like Kedar’s tents, like Solomon’s curtains.

s: Beloved has part earrings (her cheeks are beautiful with them)
q: Your cheeks are beautiful with earrings, your neck with strings of jewels.

s: Beloved has possession myrrh sachet (Lover is likened to it, lying between her breasts)
q: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh, that lies between my breasts.

s: Lover is likened to henna blossoms (from the vineyards of En Gedi)
q: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms from the vineyards of En Gedi.

s: Lover has love quality better than wine (stated by Beloved)
q: for your love is better than wine.

s: Lover is loved by virgins (because of his name)
q: Your name is oil poured out, therefore the virgins love you.

s: Beloved has relationship with daughters of Jerusalem (addresses them)
q: I am dark, but lovely, you daughters of Jerusalem

s: Lover compares beloved to steed in Pharaoh’s chariots (calls her my love)
q: I have compared you, my love, to a steed in Pharaoh’s chariots.

s: Solomon is author of Song of songs (the song is Solomon’s)
q: The Song of songs, which is Solomon’s.

s: Beloved has role keeper of the vineyards (assigned by her brothers)
q: They made me keeper of the vineyards.

s: Beloved has relationship with mother's sons (Beloved's brothers) (they were angry with her)
q: My mother’s sons were angry with me.

s: Beloved does not keep vineyards (her own vineyard)
q: I haven’t kept my own vineyard.

s: Beloved loves Lover (calls him the one her soul loves)
q: Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where you graze your flock

s: Lover has possession flock (Lover's flock) (grazes it and rests it at noon)
q: where you graze your flock, where you rest them at noon

s: Lover is brought into his rooms (by the king)
q: The king has brought me into his rooms.

s: Lover has attribute beautiful (stated by Beloved)
q: Behold, you are beautiful, my beloved, yes, pleasant; and our couch is verdant.

s: Beloved has attribute beautiful (stated by Lover)
q: Behold, you are beautiful, my love. Behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are like doves.

s: Lover is a rose of Sharon (self-description)
q: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.

s: Beloved has fruit taste sweet (to the Lover's taste)
q: his fruit was sweet to my taste.

s: Lover addresses daughters of Jerusalem (adjures them not to stir up love)
q: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires.

s: daughters of Jerusalem is located in Jerusalem
q: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem

s: Beloved has voice quality sweet (Lover's description of the beloved's voice)
q: for your voice is sweet and your face is lovely.

s: Beloved has appearance lovely (face)
q: for your voice is sweet and your face is lovely.

s: Beloved is called dove (in the clefts of the rock)
q: My dove in the clefts of the rock, in the hiding places of the mountainside

s: wall belongs to Lover (shared, "our wall"; Beloved stands behind it)
q: Behold, he stands behind our wall!

s: Lover is a lily of the valleys (self-description)
q: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.

s: Lover is like lily among thorns (compared to the daughters, said by Beloved)
q: As a lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.

s: Beloved is like apple tree among the trees of the wood (compared to the sons, said by Lover)
q: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons.

s: Beloved is like roe or young deer (Lover's comparison)
q: My beloved is like a roe or a young deer.

s: Lover belongs to Beloved (mutual belonging)
q: My beloved is mine, and I am his.

s: Beloved belongs to Lover (mutual belonging)
q: My beloved is mine, and I am his.

s: Beloved has banner love (over the Lover)
q: His banner over me is love.

s: Lover has state faint with love
q: for I am faint with love.

s: the speaker (narrator, 'my soul') loves the beloved (him whom my soul loves)
q: I sought him whom my soul loves.

s: Solomon has title King
q: King Solomon made himself a carriage

s: Solomon has mother Solomon's mother (she crowned him)
q: with the crown with which his mother has crowned him

s: Solomon's wedding day is a day of gladness of Solomon's heart
q: in the day of his weddings, in the day of the gladness of his heart.

s: carriage (Solomon's carriage) belongs to Solomon
q: Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage!

s: carriage (Solomon's carriage) has guards mighty men of Israel (guards around Solomon's carriage) (sixty of them surround it)
q: Sixty mighty men are around it, of the mighty men of Israel.

s: carriage (Solomon's carriage) made of wood of Lebanon (main material)
q: King Solomon made himself a carriage of the wood of Lebanon.

s: carriage (Solomon's carriage) has pillars of silver
q: He made its pillars of silver

s: carriage (Solomon's carriage) has bottom of gold
q: its bottom of gold

s: carriage (Solomon's carriage) has seat of purple
q: its seat of purple

s: mighty men of Israel (guards around Solomon's carriage) skilled in war (expert; all handle the sword)
q: They all handle the sword, and are expert in war.

s: mighty men of Israel (guards around Solomon's carriage) carries sword (on his thigh, because of fear in the night)
q: Every man has his sword on his thigh, because of fear in the night.

s: beloved (the bride's lover) has feature eyes like doves (behind her veil)
q: Your eyes are like doves behind your veil.

s: beloved (the bride's lover) is a sister (term of endearment)
q: You have ravished my heart, my sister, my bride.

s: beloved (the bride's lover) has attribute honey and milk under her tongue
q: Honey and milk are under your tongue.

s: beloved (the bride's lover) has attribute garments smelling like Lebanon
q: The smell of your garments is like the smell of Lebanon.

s: beloved (the bride's lover) has feature lips that drip like the honeycomb
q: Your lips, my bride, drip like the honeycomb.

s: beloved (the bride's lover) is a locked up garden (metaphor)
q: My sister, my bride, is a locked up garden; a locked up spring, a sealed fountain.

s: Lover has relationship to beloved (the bride's lover) (calls her his bride and sister)
q: You have ravished my heart, my sister, my bride.

s: Lover plans to go to mountain of myrrh (until the day is cool)
q: I will go to the mountain of myrrh, to the hill of frankincense.
